title: Improving Representation of High-frequency Components for Medical Visual Foundation Models (Frepa)
mechanism: MAE-style pretraining with high-frequency masking, low-frequency perturbation and embedding consistency so the encoder represents fine high-frequency detail; extended to Swin and ConvNets.
adaptation: Cracks are high-frequency dark lines; scuffs, source contrast and style are low-frequency. Run Frepa's ConvNeXt variant on the de-duplicated pool at 512 px 1-ch; the low-frequency perturbation doubles as source/scuff invariance for E1. PF fine-tune in U-Net++. Code reported by web search at github.com/arturia-pendragon-iris/frepa (not opened).
min_experiment: ConvNeXt Frepa pretraining on 11.9k (~40 GPU-h) + PF vs ConvNeXt ImageNet PF; out-of-fold relF1@2, E1 crack recall, inactive IoU; kill if all below +0.01.
evidence: R: 9 modalities, 32 downstream tasks; up to +15% Dice on retinal vessels over other SSL.
prior_overlap: none: our MIM used pixel targets on R34; frequency-targeted pretraining untested.

alt_notes.adaptation: Cracks are high-frequency dark lines a few px wide; scuff, contrast and source effects are low-frequency. Pretrain ConvNeXt-T (and R34 as a cheap control) on the de-duplicated 11.9k pool at 512 px, 1-ch; low-frequency perturbation doubles as source / scuff invariance for E1. PF fine-tune in smp U-Net++.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: ConvNeXt-T U-Net++ from Frepa-style continued pretraining (~100 epochs, 11.9k), PF. Baseline: ConvNeXt-T ImageNet init, PF. Metrics: cv5v2 out-of-fold crack relF1@2, E1 crack recall, inactive IoU, 2 seeds. Kill if all three < +0.01.
